Answer to round 3's F-U10a request, now settled on N10a-01's side: law-suite controls follow BD-025's per-control features (N10a-01 section 6: `cargo test -p <crate> --features <feature> --test laws_c<nn>`, one control per build; `--features gauntlet-mutations,<feature>` while staged in frob-conformance). The mutation guard as written ('a build with any nc-* feature and without gauntlet-mutations is a compile error') makes every such owning-crate run a compile error, since gauntlet-mutations is a feature of frob-conformance only and is not in a `-p <crate>` build. Restate the guard so it holds in both builds (for example keyed on the crate's own declaration: each mutation feature implies the crate's `conformance` feature, and a release build or a product binary with either is refused), and state that a `mutation` control whose target is a law suite is run by building that suite with its feature.
